subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Decimals and Measurement
seo_title: P5 Decimals and Measurement Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Multiplying and dividing decimals (up to 3 decimal places) by 10, 100, 1000 and their multiples; converting measurements between units in decimal form
meta_desc: Free P5 maths practice: × and ÷ decimals by 10, 100, 1000 and multiples, and converting km, m, kg, ℓ and ml as decimals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: × 10, 100, 1000 moves every digit 1, 2, 3 places left; ÷ moves them right.
body_html:
Move the digits, not the decimal point

When you multiply by 10, 100 or 1000, every digit moves 1, 2 or 3 places to the left. When you divide, every digit moves to the right. The number of zeros tells you how many places.

× and ÷ by multiples of 10, 100 and 1000

Split the multiple: 30 = 3 × 10, 400 = 4 × 100. Multiply or divide by the single digit first, then by 10, 100 or 1000.

Example 1

8.4 ÷ 20

20 = 2 × 10. 8.4 ÷ 2 = 4.2. Then 4.2 ÷ 10 = 0.42.

Answer: 0.42

Converting units

Learn the four facts. To change a big unit to a small unit, multiply. To change a small unit to a big unit, divide.

FactBig → small (×)Small → big (÷)
1 km = 1000 m2.35 km = 2350 m450 m = 0.45 km
1 m = 100 cm1.6 m = 160 cm85 cm = 0.85 m
1 kg = 1000 g0.3 kg = 300 g450 g = 0.45 kg
1 ℓ = 1000 ml1.25 ℓ = 1250 ml60 ml = 0.06 ℓ

Compound units as decimals

Change the small unit to a decimal of the big unit, then add the whole number.

Example 2

Write 5.07 m in m and cm.

5.07 m = 5 m + 0.07 m. 0.07 × 100 = 7, so 0.07 m = 7 cm.

Answer: 5 m 7 cm

Word problems: use the same unit

Draw a bar model. Change all the measurements to the same unit before you add or subtract.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3.5 ÷ 100 = 350 (moving the digits the wrong way)Dividing makes it smaller: 0.035
0.67 × 10 = 0.670 (“just add a zero”)Move every digit 1 place to the left: 6.7
0.45 × 30 = 1.35 (forgetting the × 10)× 3, then × 10: 13.5
3 ℓ 40 ml = 3.4 ℓ40 ml = 0.04 ℓ, so 3.04 ℓ
4.5 m = 45 cm (1 m = 10 cm)1 m = 100 cm, so 450 cm
2.4 km + 650 m = 652.4 kmSame unit first: 2.4 km + 0.65 km = 3.05 km

faq.q: What is taught in P5 decimals?
faq.a: In Primary 5, students multiply and divide decimals (up to 3 decimal places) by 10, 100, 1000 and their multiples, such as 0.45 × 30 and 8.4 ÷ 20. They also convert measurements between units in decimal form, such as 2.35 km = 2350 m and 3 ℓ 40 ml = 3.04 ℓ.

faq.q: How do I explain multiplying a decimal by 30 to my child?
faq.a: Split 30 into 3 × 10: multiply by 3 first, then by 10. For 0.45 × 30, 0.45 × 3 = 1.35 and 1.35 × 10 = 13.5.

faq.q: Why is 3 ℓ 40 ml equal to 3.04 ℓ and not 3.4 ℓ?
faq.a: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 40 ml = 40 ÷ 1000 ℓ = 0.04 ℓ, and 3 ℓ 40 ml = 3.04 ℓ. 3.4 ℓ would be 3 ℓ 400 ml.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Multiplying and dividing decimals by 10, 100, 1000 and their multiples, and converting measurements in decimal form, are part of the Primary 5 Decimals topic in the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus. These skills are used again in Primary 6 and the PSLE.

items.q: The chart shows 5.8 × 10. What is the answer?
items.e: 5.8 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 5.8 × 10 = 58. 5.80 is wrong: a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value.

items.q: The chart shows 9.4 ÷ 10. What is the answer?
items.e: 9.4 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 9.4 ÷ 10 = 0.94. 94 moves the digits the wrong way: dividing by 10 makes the number smaller.
0.67 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.67 × 100 = 67. 0.6700 only adds zeros, so it is still 0.67.
35.2 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 35.2 ÷ 100 = 0.352. 3520 moves the digits the wrong way.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 1 place to the left, so the number was multiplied by 10. 3.14 × 10 = 31.4.

items.q: Which calculation does the chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the number was divided by 100. 52.6 ÷ 100 = 0.526.
0.3 ÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 0.3 ÷ 10 = 0.03. 0.30 only adds a zero, so it is still 0.3.
4.08 × 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 4.08 × 100 = 408. Keep the 0 that holds the tens place: 408, not 48.

items.q: In 0.72 ÷ 1000, how do the digits move?
items.e: 1000 has 3 zeros, so every digit moves 3 places. Dividing makes the number smaller, so they move to the right.
2.5 × 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 2.5 × 1000 = 2500. 250 moves the digits only 2 places.
76 ÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places, starting with the ones. 76 ÷ 1000 = 0.076. 0.76 moves the digits only 2 places.

items.q: The chart shows 0.059 × 100 = 5.9. What is the value of the red digit in the answer?
items.e: The 9 was in the thousandths place. Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 9 is now in the tenths place. Its value is 9 tenths = 0.9.

items.q: The chart shows 6.43 ÷ 10 = 0.643. What is the value of the red digit in the answer?
items.e: The 3 was in the hundredths place. Every digit moved 1 place to the right, so the 3 is now in the thousandths place. Its value is 3 thousandths = 0.003.
13.07 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. The decimal point stays still. 13.07 × 10 = 130.7. 130.07 only multiplies the whole-number part. Every digit must move, including the 7.
980 ÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right. The decimal point stays still. 980 ÷ 100 = 9.8. 98 moves the digits only 1 place. The last 0 is not needed after the point: 9.80 = 9.8.
0.009 × 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. 0.009 × 1000 = 9. 0.9 moves the digit only 2 places.
The 8 moves from the tenths to the tens: that is 2 places to the left, so the missing number is 100. 79.2 is 80 − 0.8, which is subtraction, not multiplication.
The 4 moves from the ones to the thousandths: 3 places to the right. So the missing number is 1000.
Use the inverse: 62 ÷ 1000 = 0.062. Check: 0.062 × 1000 = 62. 62 000 multiplies instead of dividing.

72.5 × 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. The decimal point stays still. Write 0 in the empty places up to the ones. 72.5 × 1000 = 72 500. 7250 moves the digits only 2 places. 72 500 has 5 digits, so it is written with a space.

items.q: The steps show 0.45 × 30. What is 0.45 × 30?
The steps show 8.4 ÷ 20. What is 8.4 ÷ 20?
items.e: 20 is 2 × 10. So 8.4 ÷ 20 = 8.4 ÷ 2 ÷ 10. First 8.4 ÷ 2 = 4.2. Then 4.2 ÷ 10 = 0.42. 4.2 forgets the ÷ 10 step. 168 multiplies instead of dividing.
20 is 2 × 10. So 0.3 × 20 = 0.3 × 2 × 10. First 0.3 × 2 = 0.6. Then 0.6 × 10 = 6. 0.6 forgets the × 10 step. 20.3 adds instead of multiplying.
400 is 4 × 100. So 36 ÷ 400 = 36 ÷ 4 ÷ 100. First 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Then 9 ÷ 100 = 0.09. 0.9 divides by 40 instead of 400. 9 forgets the ÷ 100 step.

items.q: Which gives the same answer as 0.7 × 60?
The steps show 7.2 ÷ 800. What is 7.2 ÷ 800?
items.e: 800 is 8 × 100. So 7.2 ÷ 800 = 7.2 ÷ 8 ÷ 100. First 7.2 ÷ 8 = 0.9. Then 0.9 ÷ 100 = 0.009. 0.09 moves the digit only 1 place in the ÷ 100 step.
0.7 × 3 = 2.1, and 2.1 × 10 = 21. So 0.7 × 30 = 21. The missing number is 30. 20.3 is 21 − 0.7, which is subtraction.
Use the inverse: 0.06 × 40 = 0.06 × 4 × 10 = 0.24 × 10 = 2.4. Check: 2.4 ÷ 40 = 0.06. 0.0015 divides instead of multiplying.

items.q: Jun Jie says 0.25 × 80 = 2. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 80 is 8 × 10. So 0.25 × 80 = 0.25 × 8 × 10. First 0.25 × 8 = 2. Then 2 × 10 = 20. Jun Jie forgot the × 10 step.

items.q: Mei Ling says 9.6 ÷ 30 = 3.2. What is the correct answer?

items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. To change km to m, multiply by 1000: 2.35 × 1000 = 2350. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.35 km = 2350 m. 235 m uses 1 km = 100 m, which is wrong.
1 m = 100 cm. To change m to cm, multiply by 100: 4.5 × 100 = 450. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 4.5 m = 450 cm. 45 cm uses 1 m = 10 cm, which is wrong.
1 kg = 1000 g. To change g to kg, divide by 1000: 450 ÷ 1000 = 0.45. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 450 g = 0.45 kg. 4.5 kg divides by 100 instead of 1000.
1 ℓ = 1000 ml. To change ℓ to ml, multiply by 1000: 1.2 × 1000 = 1200. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.2 ℓ = 1200 ml. 120 ml multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.
1 ℓ = 1000 ml. To change ml to ℓ, divide by 1000: 750 ÷ 1000 = 0.75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 ml = 0.75 ℓ. 750 ml is less than 1 ℓ, so the answer must be less than 1.
1 km = 1000 m. To change km to m, multiply by 1000: 0.6 × 1000 = 600. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.6 km = 600 m. 60 m multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.

items.q: 5 cm = ? m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. To change cm to m, divide by 100: 5 ÷ 100 = 0.05. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 5 cm = 0.05 m. 0.5 m uses 1 m = 10 cm: 0.5 m is 50 cm.

items.q: 40 g = ? kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. To change g to kg, divide by 1000: 40 ÷ 1000 = 0.04. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 40 g = 0.04 kg. 0.4 kg divides by 100 instead of 1000: 0.4 kg is 400 g.

items.q: 86 cm = ? m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. To change cm to m, divide by 100: 86 ÷ 100 = 0.86. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 86 cm = 0.86 m. 8.6 m uses 1 m = 10 cm. 8600 m moves the digits the wrong way.
1 m = 100 cm. To change m to cm, multiply by 100: 0.75 × 100 = 75. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 0.75 m = 75 cm. 7.5 cm uses 1 m = 10 cm.

items.q: Which mass is equal to 0.8 kg?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. To change kg to g, multiply by 1000: 0.8 × 1000 = 800. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.8 kg = 800 g. 80 g multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.

items.q: What is the mass shown on the scale, in grams?
items.e: The needle is 4 small marks past 1 kg. Each small mark is 0.1 kg, so the mass is 1.4 kg. 1 kg = 1000 g. To change kg to g, multiply by 1000: 1.4 × 1000 = 1400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.4 kg = 1400 g. 1040 g is 1 kg 40 g, not 1 kg 400 g.

items.q: How much water is in the jug, in litres?
items.e: The water is at 600 ml. 1 ℓ = 1000 ml. To change ml to ℓ, divide by 1000: 600 ÷ 1000 = 0.6. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 600 ml = 0.6 ℓ. 6 ℓ divides by 100 instead of 1000.
1 kg = 1000 g. To change kg to g, multiply by 1000: 3.08 × 1000 = 3080. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.08 kg = 3080 g. 3800 g drops the 0 that holds the tenths place: 3.08 is not 3.8.
1 km = 1000 m. To change m to km, divide by 1000: 2050 ÷ 1000 = 2.05. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 2050 m = 2.05 km. 2.5 km drops the 0 that holds the tenths place: 2.5 km is 2500 m.
1 ℓ = 1000 ml. To change ℓ to ml, multiply by 1000: 0.025 × 1000 = 25. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.025 ℓ = 25 ml. 250 ml reads 0.025 as 0.25.
1 ℓ = 1000 ml. To change ml to ℓ, divide by 1000: 12 500 ÷ 1000 = 12.5. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 12 500 ml = 12.5 ℓ. 125 ℓ divides by 100 instead of 1000.

items.q: Each small mark is 0.1 km. How far from 0 is the arrow, in metres?
items.e: The arrow is 4 small marks past 2 km, so it is at 2.4 km. 1 km = 1000 m. To change km to m, multiply by 1000: 2.4 × 1000 = 2400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.4 km = 2400 m. 2040 m is 2 km 40 m, not 2 km 400 m.

items.q: Which length is equal to 307 cm?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. To change cm to m, divide by 100: 307 ÷ 100 = 3.07. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 307 cm = 3.07 m. 3.7 m drops the 0 that holds the tenths place: 3.7 m is 370 cm.

items.q: Which mass is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 0.9 kg = 900 g and 0.09 kg = 90 g. 900 g is more than 899 g, 850 g and 90 g, so 0.9 kg is the heaviest.

items.q: 3 ℓ 40 ml = ? ℓ
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 40 ml = 40 ÷ 1000 ℓ = 0.04 ℓ. 3 ℓ 40 ml = 3 ℓ + 0.04 ℓ = 3.04 ℓ. 3.4 ℓ is a common mistake: 0.4 ℓ is 400 ml, not 40 ml.

items.q: 2 m 35 cm = ? m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 35 cm = 35 ÷ 100 m = 0.35 m. 2 m 35 cm = 2 m + 0.35 m = 2.35 m. 2.035 m uses 1 m = 1000 cm, which is wrong.

items.q: 5 kg 600 g = ? kg
4 km 250 m = ? km
7 m 8 cm = ? m
1 kg 5 g = ? kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so 5 g = 5 ÷ 1000 kg = 0.005 kg. 1 kg 5 g = 1 kg + 0.005 kg = 1.005 kg. 1.5 kg is 1 kg 500 g, and 1.05 kg is 1 kg 50 g. 5 g is 5 thousandths of a kilogram.

items.q: 6 ℓ 5 ml = ? ℓ
items.e: 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 5 ml = 5 ÷ 1000 ℓ = 0.005 ℓ. 6 ℓ 5 ml = 6 ℓ + 0.005 ℓ = 6.005 ℓ. 6.05 ℓ is 6 ℓ 50 ml. Two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places.

items.q: 9 kg 75 g = ? kg
2.6 ℓ = ? ℓ ? ml
items.e: 2.6 ℓ = 2 ℓ + 0.6 ℓ. 1 ℓ = 1000 ml, so 0.6 ℓ = 0.6 × 1000 ml = 600 ml. 2.6 ℓ = 2 ℓ 600 ml. 2 ℓ 6 ml is a common mistake: the 6 is 6 tenths of a litre, which is 600 ml.

items.q: 1.8 km = ? km ? m
3.45 kg = ? kg ? g
items.e: 3.45 kg = 3 kg + 0.45 kg. 1 kg = 1000 g, so 0.45 kg = 0.45 × 1000 g = 450 g. 3.45 kg = 3 kg 450 g. 3 kg 45 g treats the digits after the point as grams: 0.45 kg is 450 g, not 45 g.

items.q: 3 m 6 cm = ? cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 3 m = 300 cm. 300 cm + 6 cm = 306 cm. 360 cm is 3 m 60 cm. 36 cm uses 1 m = 10 cm.

items.q: 2 km 40 m = ? m
Each small mark is 10 cm. What length does the arrow show, in metres?
items.e: The arrow is 7 small marks past 2 m, so it shows 2 m 70 cm. 1 m = 100 cm, so 70 cm = 70 ÷ 100 m = 0.7 m. 2 m 70 cm = 2 m + 0.7 m = 2.7 m. 2.07 m is 2 m 7 cm.
The needle is 3 small marks past 2 kg, so it shows 2.3 kg. 2.3 kg = 2 kg + 0.3 kg. 1 kg = 1000 g, so 0.3 kg = 0.3 × 1000 g = 300 g. 2.3 kg = 2 kg 300 g. 2 kg 30 g is 2.03 kg.

items.q: Which mass is equal to 4.06 kg?
items.e: 4.06 kg = 4 kg + 0.06 kg. 1 kg = 1000 g, so 0.06 kg = 0.06 × 1000 g = 60 g. 4.06 kg = 4 kg 60 g. 4 kg 600 g is 4.6 kg. 406 g multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.

items.q: Siti says 6 m 5 cm = 6.5 m. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 5 cm = 5 ÷ 100 m = 0.05 m. 6 m 5 cm = 6 m + 0.05 m = 6.05 m. 6.5 m is 6 m 50 cm, so Siti is wrong.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 2.5 m = 250 cm, 2 m 45 cm = 245 cm, 2.05 m = 205 cm. So 255 cm is the longest.
Change 350 g to kilograms first: 350 ÷ 1000 = 0.35 kg. 1.2 kg + 0.35 kg = 1.55 kg. 4.7 kg uses 1 kg = 100 g. 351.2 kg adds numbers with different units. 15.5 kg puts the point in the wrong place.

items.q: A packet of rice has a mass of 2.5 kg. Mrs Lim buys 10 packets for a food donation drive. What is the total mass of the rice?
items.e: 2.5 × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left. 2.5 × 10 = 25 kg. 12.5 kg adds 10 instead of multiplying. 2.50 kg only adds a zero.

items.q: Wei Ming’s school is 1.35 km from his HDB flat. How far is that in metres?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. To change km to m, multiply by 1000: 1.35 × 1000 = 1350. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.35 km = 1350 m. 1035 m is 1 km 35 m.

items.q: One lap of the school field is 400 m. Hafiz runs 8 laps on Sports Day. How far does he run, in kilometres?
A plate of chicken rice at a hawker centre costs $4.50. Mr Tan buys 30 plates for a staff lunch. How much does he pay?
A stack of 100 exercise books has a mass of 18.5 kg. What is the mass of 1 exercise book, in grams?
items.e: 18.5 ÷ 100 = 0.185 kg. 0.185 × 1000 = 185 g. 0.185 g forgets to change kg to g. 1850 g divides by 10 instead of 100.

items.q: For a recycling drive, 1000 students each bring 0.45 kg of old newspapers. What is the total mass?
items.e: 0.45 × 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left. 0.45 × 1000 = 450 kg. 45 kg moves the digits only 2 places. 1000.45 kg adds.

items.q: A jug holds 2.4 ℓ of lime juice. It is poured equally into 20 cups for a class party. How much juice is in each cup, in millilitres?
items.e: 20 units = 2.4 ℓ, so 1 unit = 2.4 ℓ ÷ 20 = 0.12 ℓ. 0.12 × 1000 = 120 ml. 0.12 ml forgets to change litres to millilitres. 1200 ml divides by 2 instead of 20.

items.q: A jar of kaya has a mass of 0.35 kg. The school canteen buys 40 jars. What is the total mass?
items.e: 40 is 4 × 10. So 0.35 × 40 = 0.35 × 4 × 10. First 0.35 × 4 = 1.4. Then 1.4 × 10 = 14. The total mass is 14 kg. 12 kg uses 0.3 instead of 0.35.

items.q: A tap lets out 0.6 ℓ of water every minute. How much water does it let out in 30 minutes?
items.e: 30 is 3 × 10. So 0.6 × 30 = 0.6 × 3 × 10. First 0.6 × 3 = 1.8. Then 1.8 × 10 = 18. It lets out 18 ℓ. 30.6 ℓ adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: A rope 5.6 m long is cut into 70 equal pieces for a CCA craft session. How long is each piece, in centimetres?
items.e: 70 is 7 × 10. So 5.6 ÷ 70 = 5.6 ÷ 7 ÷ 10. First 5.6 ÷ 7 = 0.8. Then 0.8 ÷ 10 = 0.08. Each piece is 0.08 m. 0.08 × 100 = 8 cm. 80 cm forgets the ÷ 10 step. 0.08 cm forgets to change m to cm.

items.q: Each durian has a mass of 1 kg 750 g. Mr Rahman buys 10 durians of the same mass. What is the total mass, in kilograms?
items.e: 1 kg 750 g = 1.75 kg. 10 units = 1.75 kg × 10 = 17.5 kg. 10.75 kg uses 1 kg 750 g = 1.075 kg. 1.75 kg is the mass of one durian.

items.q: Ali cycles 2.4 km at East Coast Park. Then he cycles another 650 m. How far does he cycle in all, in kilometres?
items.e: 650 m = 0.65 km. 2.4 km + 0.65 km = 3.05 km. 3.5 km drops the 0 in the tenths place. 8.9 km uses 650 m = 6.5 km. 652.4 km adds numbers with different units.

items.q: A red ribbon is 2.45 m long. A blue ribbon is 80 cm shorter. How long is the blue ribbon, in metres?
items.e: 80 cm = 0.8 m. 2.45 m − 0.8 m = 1.65 m. 2.37 m uses 80 cm = 0.08 m. 3.25 m adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: Mrs Ng pays $72 for 800 red packets for Chinese New Year at his office. All the red packets cost the same. How much does 1 red packet cost?
items.e: 800 is 8 × 100. So 72 ÷ 800 = 72 ÷ 8 ÷ 100. First 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Then 9 ÷ 100 = 0.09. So 1 red packet costs $0.09 (9¢). $0.90 divides by 80 instead of 800. $0.72 divides by 100 only.

items.q: Xin Yi drinks 1.25 ℓ of water in a day. Zhi Hao drinks 950 ml. How much more water does Xin Yi drink, in millilitres?
items.e: 1.25 ℓ = 1250 ml. 1250 ml − 950 ml = 300 ml. 825 ml uses 1.25 ℓ = 125 ml. 948.75 ml subtracts numbers with different units.

items.q: Mdm Wong packs 8.4 kg of rambutans equally into 30 bags. What is the mass of each bag, in grams?
items.e: 30 is 3 × 10. So 8.4 ÷ 30 = 8.4 ÷ 3 ÷ 10. First 8.4 ÷ 3 = 2.8. Then 2.8 ÷ 10 = 0.28. Each bag is 0.28 kg. 0.28 × 1000 = 280 g. 2800 g forgets the ÷ 10 step. 0.28 g forgets to change kg to g.

items.q: Chloe has a ribbon 3 m long. She cuts 20 pieces, each 12 cm long, to make bookmarks. How much ribbon is left, in metres?
items.e: Used: 20 × 12 cm = 240 cm = 2.4 m. Left: 3 m − 2.4 m = 0.6 m. 2.4 m is the ribbon used, not left. 2.88 m takes away only 1 piece (12 cm). 0.06 m is 6 cm.

items.q: Raju walks 0.75 km from his flat to the MRT station every morning, and walks back home in the evening. How far does he walk on these trips in 20 days?
items.e: Each day: 0.75 km × 2 = 1.5 km. In 20 days: 1.5 × 20 = 1.5 × 2 × 10 = 3 × 10 = 30 km. 15 km forgets the walk back.

items.q: For a picnic at the Botanic Gardens, Ethan buys 3 bottles of water of 1.5 ℓ each and 4 cans of juice of 330 ml each. How much drink does he buy in all, in litres?
items.e: Water: 1.5 ℓ × 3 = 4.5 ℓ. Juice: 330 ml × 4 = 1320 ml = 1.32 ℓ. Total: 4.5 ℓ + 1.32 ℓ = 5.82 ℓ. 17.7 ℓ uses 1 ℓ = 100 ml. 4.83 ℓ adds just one can.

items.q: Priya has a 1.5 ℓ bottle of soya bean milk. She pours out 350 ml for her brother. How much soya bean milk is left, in litres?
items.e: 350 ml = 0.35 ℓ. 1.5 ℓ − 0.35 ℓ = 1.15 ℓ. 1.85 ℓ adds instead of subtracting. 1.465 ℓ uses 350 ml = 0.035 ℓ. 1150 ℓ forgets to change 1150 ml back to litres.
